title: PLACE: Prompt Learning for Attributed Community Search in Large Graphs

problem.claim: Attributed Community Search aims to identify communities in attributed graphs that are structurally cohesive and attribute-homogeneous for given queries.

gap.claim: Existing graph refinements are detached from end-to-end backbone optimization or impose additional training-resource burdens, limiting adaptability and practical usage across diverse graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Attributed Community Search seeks structurally cohesive and attribute-homogeneous communities for given queries.
Learning-based approaches use GNNs to model structural and attribute information, with input-graph and query refinements such as node pruning and feature enhancement.
These refinements may be disconnected from end-to-end optimization or increase training-resource demands, reducing adaptability and practical usage.

unknowns: The proposed method and its concrete contributions are not stated.
No experiments, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are supplied.
No explicit novelty claim is supplied.
